title: Committing to a direct attack

D0.outcome: Explains that a direct attack, once started, needs every available piece and certainty, and that stopping halfway can be worse than not starting.

D1.outcome: Counts the pieces available and decides whether every piece can be brought in.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, decides to continue, break off or accept a repetition, and avoids starting without enough force.

D3.outcome: Tests whether breaking off or repeating is better than pressing on, and predicts which piece, coming in last, decides.

misconceptions: Never break off a direct attack.
Start an attack because the king looks weak.
conditions: Enough force to be sure; every available piece is brought in, and the last piece often decides.
The simple winning move may be preferable until experience allows the complication.
contrasts: 'never break off' is absolute; engines often show that regrouping or a repetition is better.
Starting an attack because the king looks weak, without counting the pieces.
A position where the simple winning move exists.
